newsitem.title: USA: Investigators find Hamas link to NY suspects.
newsitem.headline: Investigators find Hamas link to NY suspects.

text.p: Investigators have evidence linking suspects in an alleged New York suicide bombing plot to the radical Palestinian group Hamas, a law enforcement source said on Friday.

The source said investigators believed that the suspects arrested in a police raid on a Brooklyn apartment at dawn on Thursday made telephone calls to the organisation from a grocery store and a laundromat in the neighbourhood.
Hamas claimed responsibility for the double suicide bombing in a Jerusalem market Wednesday that killed 13 people and wounded 170 others.
New York City and federal officials had earlier said there was no evidence linking the suspects to the Jerusalem bombing.

Two suspects were named in federal court documents as Gazi Ibrahim Abu Mezer, 23 and Lafi Khalil, 22. It said Abu Mezer had allegedly been accused in Israel "of being a member of a known terrorist organisation." It did not name the group.

"The suspects were using the telephones at the laundromat and grocery store near the apartment where they were staying and we were able to trace the numbers back to Hamas," the law enforcement source told Reuters.
In the West Bank, relatives said the two men had gone to the United States to live the "American Dream" and doubted they were involved in the alleged plot.

Police shot and wounded Khalil and Abu Mezer in the apartment raid after one of them lunged for one of the pipe bombs, authorities said. The federal complaint said Abu Mezer later told police the bombs were intended for detonation on the subway.
A third man was being held for questioning, officials said.
A man living in the same apartment tipped police officers about the explosives on Wednesday night, police sources said.

"It looks like they were going to set off a suicide bomb and try to make the point that the United States and Israel are wrong and strike against U.S. and Jewish interests," New York City Mayor Rudolph Giuliani said on Friday.

Four of the devices removed from the apartment by police bomb disposal experts were pipe bombs strapped together and they contained black powder or nails with wires and switches, according to police sources.

Security was tightened around New York on Friday in moves that were were reminiscent of the aftermath of the February 1993 bombing of the World Trade Centre by Moslem militants in which six people were killed and more than 1,000 injured.

Major subway, regional rail and bus stations, government buildings, courthouses, diplomatic offices, synagogues and mosques were among the places where police officers and security guards were seen in greater numbers.

"There are extra police and extra patrols in places that the police department and the FBI might consider sensitive areas ... I would not call it an alert," Giuliani told WCBS News in a radio interview.
In Washington, President Bill Clinton praised police but said it was too early to draw conclusions about the case.

"We have worked very hard in this country to increase our capacity to deal with terrorism, it is something we take very seriously, and we will continue to do that," Clinton told reporters at the White House.
